input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: § 12.4 binds us (Customer) with a non-compete that survives 24 months post-term, covers any competing product or service, and applies in any territory, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (indeed it expressly bars acquisitions). That is walk-away territory under the rule: post-term restriction longer than 12 months and undefined scope, well short of the fallback (named competing product, term only, 12-month cap, internal development/acquisition carve-outs). It also directly conflicts with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. Redline deletes § 12.4 to reach the preferred position, with the narrowed fallback offered in the comment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept any restriction on the businesses we operate or the products we develop, buy or sell, so we have deleted the 24-month worldwide non-compete; it also contradicts § 12.3, which confirms we have given no non-compete commitment. If you need protection, we could consider a term-only restriction on a single named competing product, capped at 12 months with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Delete the 24-month post-term worldwide non-compete binding Customer.
